# A grid in a popup renders no cells: engine scrollLeft 762, DOM at 0

## Context

Found by the operator's manual walk of `apps/workstation` on the v13.3.1 candidate (`dev` 0ab667195e), 2026-10-23 ~20:2xZ, while repeating #20009's dock gestures on the 100k Matrix pane (no worker freeze reproduced). The Matrix pane sits alone in a popup window (320 × 270 CSS px inner); the grid shows its header (*Living signal*, *Action*) and an empty body. The operator expects a small popup resize to repair it; the live reads below were taken before any resize.

Live reads through the Neural Link at 20:25Z (session `966a2f3e…`, popup window `3e000f5f…`):

- `neo-grid-body-1` (`Neo.grid.Body`, mounted): `containerWidth: 320`, `availableWidth: 1080` (eight columns), **`scrollLeft: 762`**, `visibleColumns: [5, 7]`, `bufferColumnRange: 2`, `scrollTop: 0`, `availableHeight: 185`, `availableRows: 3`, `rowHeight: 50`; `wrapperStyle {flex: '1 1 0%'}`.
- `neo-grid-header-toolbar-1` (`Neo.grid.header.Toolbar`): **`scrollLeft: 762`** as well.
- The rows exist. Row 0's vdom: cells 0–2 carry `style.display: 'none'`; cells 3–7 are laid out at `left` 380, 510, 640, 790, 950 px. The DOM rects of the cell components prove the DOM scroll is **0**: `neo-progress-1` (the progress cell, `left: 640`) sits at viewport x = 651, `neo-sparkline-1` at 801, `neo-button-42` at 965, all beyond the 318-px viewport; the header toolbar's DOM shows the first two columns at x 1–319.
- 762 is exactly `1080 − 318`, the far-right scroll limit of this viewport: the engine's position is one this window's viewport can reach, and the DOM is not there.
- No console error in the session.

So the body computed its column window from an engine `scrollLeft` (762) the window's DOM does not hold (0): the cells inside the viewport are the hidden ones, the rendered ones are off-screen, and the body reads as empty.

## The Problem

`Neo.grid.Body#updateMountedAndVisibleColumns` derives `visibleColumns` from `me.scrollLeft` (`src/grid/Body.mjs` around line 1565) and `afterSetScrollLeft` is its only trigger; the config is normally fed from the DOM's scroll events through the scroll sync. Two candidate ways for the config and the DOM to part, to be decided by the operator's sequence (asked) and a resize of the popup (asked, with a re-read):

- **(A) a remount after a horizontal scroll.** The grid was scrolled to the far right in the popup, then a gesture re-projected the popup and re-mounted the grid; the new DOM element starts at `scrollLeft` 0, no scroll event fires, and `Body#afterSetMounted` re-arms only the scroll edge (`src/grid/Body.mjs` ~538), re-syncing nothing horizontal. Prior art: on a pop-out hop the vertical pair reset together, config and DOM both to 0, with the writer of that 0 unverified (Mnemosyne's receipt on Discussion #18224, 2026-09-04); the horizontal pair has no such reset.
- **(B) a commanded scroll the DOM never confirmed.** `Neo.grid.header.Toolbar#scrollToIndex` (the column-drag overdrag loop) writes `scrollLeft` optimistically, command-driven, "not yet confirmed" until the DOM scroll reports (`src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs` ~55–197, ~494–533); if the `DomAccess.scrollTo` command reached a window other than the popup, or the confirmation never came back, the engine keeps the commanded value while the popup's DOM stays at 0. The windowId class of #18291 (cells kept the opener's windowId after a hop) is the precedent for a command addressed to the wrong window.

Observation vs inference: the stale pair is measured; which of (A) or (B) produced it is inference until the sequence is known.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/Body.mjs`: `scrollLeft_` config (~206), `afterSetScrollLeft` → `updateMountedAndVisibleColumns` (~582, ~1561–1590), `afterSetMounted` (~538); `scrollTop` is "controlled externally by Grid.Container.syncBodies()" (~587) and resets with the DOM on remount; `scrollLeft` has no remount hook.
- `src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs`: the command-driven `scrollLeft` during a column drag (~55, ~89, ~180–197, `scrollToIndex` ~494).
- The horizontal scroll sync addon feeds the body's and the header's `scrollLeft` from the DOM scroll events (`ScrollManager.syncGridBody`, main-thread `GridHorizontalScrollSync`); on a fresh DOM in a popup there is no event until the user scrolls.
- Prior art: Discussion #18224 (popup-birth arm receipts), #18291 (`grid.Row` without `afterSetWindowId`), #19998 (the Matrix grid keeps a window-sized viewport and row pool whatever its ancestors do).

Design authority: the grid's own contract that `visibleColumns` describes the DOM's viewport; the body and the DOM must agree on `scrollLeft` after any remount or commanded scroll.

## The Fix

1. Record the operator's sequence on this ticket and the result of the resize (does `visibleColumns` return to `[0, 1]` with `scrollLeft` 0, or does the DOM jump to 762?); that decides between (A) and (B).
2. (A): on a remount (`afterSetMounted(true)` after `false`, or a `windowId` change) re-apply the engine's `scrollLeft` to the new DOM through the scroll sync's own write path (the user's horizontal position survives the hop, as the vertical one should), or reset the config to 0 together with the DOM; either way the pair agrees. (B): the commanded scroll must address the grid's own window and the command must settle or roll back when the DOM reports nothing.
3. Red-first: a Neural Link e2e under `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/` that pops the Matrix pane out, scrolls it to the far right, performs the operator's gesture, and asserts that the body's `visibleColumns` and the DOM's scroll agree and that a cell is painted inside the viewport; a unit arm for the remount re-sync.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The operator's sequence is recorded here and reproduced red on `dev` 0ab667195e by an e2e arm (the popup's grid body with `scrollLeft` ≠ the DOM scroll and no cell inside the viewport).
- [ ] AC-2: After the fix the same arm is green: the body's `scrollLeft` equals the DOM's, `visibleColumns` covers the viewport, and at least one cell rect intersects the viewport.
- [ ] AC-3: A unit arm on `Neo.grid.Body`: a remount after a non-zero `scrollLeft` leaves the config and the (stubbed) DOM in agreement.
- [ ] AC-4: The vertical pair is measured in the PR (Discussion #18224's finding: config and DOM both reset to 0 on a hop) and either kept symmetric with the horizontal fix or recorded as a separate ticket.
- [ ] AC-5 (post-merge): the operator repeats his sequence on the merged head and the body renders its cells.

## Out of Scope

#20009 (what made the Matrix pane content-sized); the vertical scroll reset on a hop beyond its measurement (AC-4 names it); #20081.

## Measured mechanism (steward, 20:5xZ, before any resize) and the milestone call

The body's `scrollLeft` of 762 can only come from the scroll pipeline's echo of a real DOM scroll (`grid.ScrollManager#onContainerScroll`); `header.Toolbar#scrollToIndex`'s optimistic write touches only the toolbar's backing field and the SortZone term (`src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs` ~494–533), never the body. So the popup's DOM reached 762 once, and later stood at 0 without an event the engine saw. The header toolbar holds no pending command (`pendingScrollTarget` null, no drag active). Candidate (B) is out; **(A) it is: a remount, or a DOM reset of the scroll container, inside the popup after the user scrolled to the far right.** The grid container is `Workstation.view.ScalePane` (`neo-grid-container-1`, parent `neo-container-39`), window `3e000f5f…`; the state is still live in the operator's app for a setter trace (session `966a2f3e…` at 20:5xZ, ids change on his reload).

**Fix shape:** on the grid's remount path (a re-projection in the popup, or a hop between windows), re-apply the engine's horizontal position to the new DOM through `DomAccess.scrollTo` on the horizontal scrollbar with the grid's `windowId` (the path `scrollToIndex` already uses), so the body, the header and the DOM agree and the user keeps their position; or reset the body's and the header's `scrollLeft` to 0 together with the DOM. The vertical pair's reset on a hop (Discussion #18224) is the asymmetric precedent; AC-4 keeps it in view.

**Reproducer for AC-1:** pop the Matrix pane into a 320-px popup, scroll it to the far right (the horizontal scrollbar to its end), then re-project the popup (move a second tab into it, or reorder its strip), and read the pair: the body's `scrollLeft` against the DOM's, and whether a cell rect intersects the viewport. The operator's own sequence is still to be recorded here when he has it; the arm above does not depend on it.

**Milestone v13.3.1 (steward's call, delegated by the operator at 20:5xZ):** the ruling's rationale is a version with no known defect for the external tester, and an empty showcase grid after a popup gesture is that defect; the candidate moves to this fix's head and gate 2 reruns there. Assigned to Ada (handoff, hers to decline on AGENT:*).

Fix: #20083. Measured trigger: any hide and re-show (a tab switch in the Matrix's popup stack) or DOM move (a split beside it) resets the grid's scroll offsets with no scroll event while `mounted` stays `true`. Both axes desync (engine `[609, 5000]`, DOM `[0, 0]`, no cell in sight); the fix restores the engine's position on the next resize delivery.

- 2026-10-23T22:07:57Z @tobiu referenced in commit `36a74c7` - "fix(grid): a grid shown again or moved in the DOM gets its scroll position back (#20082) (#20083)

A browser resets a scroll container's offsets when it stops being laid
out (the inactive card of a tab stack) or moves in the DOM, and fires
no scroll event. The engine kept the user's position, so the bodies
rendered the rows and columns of that position into a viewport showing
the origin: the 100k Matrix grid in a popup read as empty after a dock
gesture.

grid.Container#onResize now reads the horizontal scrollbar's and the
view's offsets after each delivery, and writes the engine's position
back on an axis the DOM holds at the origin; the answering scroll keeps
the header and the bodies in step. A DOM away from the origin is a live
scroll the engine has not echoed yet, and stays untouched."
